judgment: A small fox is almost across —
image: Fire over water: Not Yet Across.
So the noble one carefully tells things apart
and puts each in its place.
lines: He is not yet across, and to march: misfortune.
Yet it is good to ford the great river.
Holding firm: good, and regret gone.
and is rewarded in three years with a great state.
Holding firm: good, and no regret.
there is trust in it. Good.
There is trust as he drinks wine: no harm.
But if he wets his head,
then, trust or not, this is lost.

notes.name_en: 未濟 the crossing not yet made; paired with 63 Already Across. Not Wilhelm's 'Before Completion'.
notes.L1: The wet tail of the judgment's fox, now in the first line; the water sequence (tail, wheels, head) mirrors 63 in reverse.
notes.L6: 有孚失是 'though there is trust, losing this (rightness)'; B makes the wet head the condition ('if he wets his head, then…').
notes.L5: 君子之光有孚: B gives the light its verb ('shines'); 有孚 then answers it ('there is trust in it').
